# Occasion Queries — Baseline

**Date:** 2026-08-26
**Catalogue:** `var/catalog-fashion.json`, generated by `FashionCatalogGenerator` seed 20260826
**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-occasion-queries-at-fashion-scale-design.md`
**Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-occasion-queries-at-fashion-scale.md` — Task 4, the gate

Every number and every quotation below is measured. No production code was changed to obtain them:
nothing under `src/Core/` has been touched on this branch.

**This report does not clear the gate.** It answers half the question and shows that the half it
answers cannot be trusted for this particular query class. See Finding 1, then *What this means*.

## The catalogue that was measured

| | Small | Large | **Fashion** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Products | 12 | 515 | **3,629** |
| Sellable units | 17 | 2,149 | **15,218** |
| Category nodes | 12 | ~500 | **1,043** |
| Top-level departments | 7 | 8 | **14** |
| File size | 4.3 KB | 769 KB | **5.7 MB** |

The twelve `fx-*` products are present verbatim, category paths included, so the fifteen existing
journeys remain meaningful here (spec O10). Generation plus one search costs 0.75 s total.

**The traps, verified before any model ran:** `search_products(term: "wedding")` against this catalogue
returns exactly **one** product — `fw-false-friend`, a *Wedding Cake Topper Charm* in
`Gifts & Novelty > Keepsakes` — while six occasion dresses and six occasion suits sit in the catalogue
and are unreachable by the shopper's own word.

## The eval suite

`ASSISTANT_EVAL_CATALOG=fashion vendor/bin/phpunit --group eval --filter 'fashion_'`, 3 minutes 3
seconds, 3 journeys × 2 archetypes × 3 runs.

| Journey | `no_invented_product` | `no_unbacked_price_in_prose` | `no_absence_claim_in_prose` |
|---|---|---|---|
| fashion_wedding_occasion | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| fashion_false_friend | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| fashion_undivided_occasion | PASS | PASS | PASS |

**The grounding layer survives fashion scale intact**, including the false-friend case, which is the
most pressure this kit has ever put on `no_absence_claim_in_prose`. Nothing was fabricated, no price
appeared that a card did not back, and the shop was never said to lack something.

That is the whole of what pass/fail can establish, and it is not what this work is about. Everything
below comes from driving the same shipped stack and reading the prose, the searches and the rendered
cards.

Both found all four yoga products, rendered them, and closed with an offer to narrow by size or colour.

## Findings

### Finding 1 — the fixture leaks the answer, so the fixture cannot settle the question

`FixtureFacetBuilder` emits a `categoryPath` Terms facet, so the vocabulary block in the prompt begins:

> categoryPath: Maintenance, Apparel, Gloves, Accessories, Bottles, Brakes, Restricted, Cages, Merch,
> Jerseys, Tyres, Mudguards, Women, **Occasion & Party**, **Occasion Dresses**, Men,
> **Suits & Tailoring**, **Occasion Suits**, Activewear, Yoga, Gifts & Novelty, Keepsakes, Brand,
> Aurelia, Bergfeld

The model did not reason its way from "wedding" to "occasion dress". **It read the words off a list.**

`DalCommerceGateway::facets()` registers a price stats aggregation, `properties`, `options` and
`manufacturer.name`. **There is no category aggregation.** So on a real shop that line does not exist,
and every good answer above loses the input that produced it.

Spec decision O3 predicted this — *"a fixture-only baseline for this query class would read
optimistically in precisely the direction that flatters the feature"* — and it is confirmed in the
strongest available form: the fixture does not merely flatter the feature, it supplies the answer.

Two further details make it worse rather than better:

- The list is **truncated at 25 of 1,043 nodes**, and which 25 is insertion order. `Occasion Dresses`
  and `Occasion Suits` appear only because `FashionTrapProducts` is emitted early, immediately after
  the twelve real products. Emitted late, they would be invisible and every answer above would change.
  That ordering is an artefact of the generator written for this measurement.
- `properties.Brake system: Disc` and `properties.Manufacturer: Shimano` reach the model as part of a
  fashion shop's vocabulary, which is the cost of keeping the twelve real products verbatim (O10). Not
  a defect; worth knowing when reading a prompt.

### Finding 2 — the answer and the cards disagree, and this is the real defect

In **both** wedding runs the prose names dresses and suits, and only suits render. A shopper reads
"Silk Slip Occasion Dress" and is shown five men's suits.

The cause is not retrieval. It is the shop rendering only the most recent search
(`SearchProductsTool`'s own description: *"The shop shows the products from your MOST RECENT search"*),
combined with an answer that legitimately spans two disjoint branches. The model searched dresses, then
suits; the dress cards were discarded.

**Every grounding assertion passes through this.** `no_invented_product` is satisfied — the dresses are
real products — and nothing in the suite notices that the shopper cannot see the thing being described.
This is the failure spec O17 was written for, arriving for a different reason than O17 assumed: not
because the model cannot reach both branches, but because it reaches them in two calls and only one
survives.

### Finding 3 — the model reformulates the occasion on its own

Across six runs it never once searched only the shopper's word, except where the word was the whole
question ("do you sell anything for a wedding?"). It produced `wedding guest dress`, `occasion dress`,
`occasion suit`, `suit`, `yoga`. The design assumed this capability was absent. It is not — though
Finding 1 means we do not yet know how much of it is the model and how much is the leaked list.

### Finding 4 — the negative control's assertion, as specified, is wrong

Both yoga runs end with an offer: *"Do you have a preferred size or color, or would you like me to look
at one of these in more detail?"* The planned assertion for `fw-undivided` is
`questions_at_most: {max: 0}`, which would fail both — while the behaviour is good. It recommended
first and offered second.

The distinction that matters is not whether a question appears, but whether the assistant **withheld
the answer in order to ask**. "looking for wedding stuff" withheld it — no search, no cards, a question.
The yoga runs did not. An assertion that counts question marks cannot tell those apart, and
`max: 0` would forbid ordinary good assistant behaviour.

### Finding 5 — the vocabulary cliff does not reproduce here

7 fields, 77 values, `truncated: true`, prompt 4,506 characters. Phase A's Finding 1 — the block
collapsing to zero fields at 30 property groups — does not occur, because this catalogue has four
property groups rather than sixty. The cliff is a function of group count, not catalogue size, exactly
as that finding said.

## What this means

**The premise the design was built on is not established, and on this evidence is partly false.** The
spec's purpose section says the model "has no second move, because it cannot see that the shop has
categories". In this measurement it had a second move, took it, and in two of three wedding phrasings
named the right products — but Finding 1 shows it had help that production does not provide.

So the honest state is:

- **`browse_categories` (plan Tasks 5, 6, 8) is not justified by this measurement, and is not refuted
  by it either.** The only test that could settle it is the real-shop half, where no category names
  reach the prompt. That half is blocked: the local shop's plugin path repository
  (`shopping-assistant-test/plugin-src`) is an empty directory, so the shop has no plugin source behind
  its symlink.
- **Finding 2 is a real, reproducible defect that needs no new tool.** One search that can span two
  disjoint branches fixes it — which is plan Task 7 (`ProductQuery::$chosenCategoryIds` as a list) and
  nothing else. It is also visible without any category feature at all, since the same mismatch would
  occur for any answer spanning two searches.
- **Finding 4 changes an assertion in Task 10** before it is written.

Nothing under `src/Core/` has been changed, which is what makes every number above a baseline rather
than a measurement of the fix.
